title: Flock Safety Shares Camera Access Across Agencies
summary: A privacy/cybersecurity firm's blog post analyzes Flock Safety's camera-sharing software architecture, describing how feature-level permissions (search, hotlist, live video, PTZ, downloads, analytics), state/radius auto-approval, nationwide discoverability, revocation, and CSV export are distinct mechanisms. It argues that 'sharing cameras' collapses meaningfully different access powers and that revocation cannot recover already-exported data.

key_quotes.quote: A camera can be owned by one organization while access to its capabilities crosses an organizational boundary through software.
The sharing workflow can translate selected product features into distinct permission sets for another organization, which makes the phrase "share cameras" too imprecise for oversight.
Discoverability can increase the population of organizations able to find and request access without itself granting that access.
Revocation runs on two clocks. It can end future access inside the service, while a CSV or downloaded recording may keep existing under the recipient's controls.
